item.title: JavaScript-heavy approaches are not compatible with long-term performance goals
item.description:
📝 Also note that I’ll be jumping between different aspects of web performance throughout the post, without much thought. In Computer Science, the commonly accepted distinction between the two is that a library is something that your code calls into, while a framework is something that you relinquish control unto, so that it calls your code instead, at the appropriate time. In short, the claim is that this approach will offer huge improvements to developer experience, and that these DevEx benefits will trickle down to the user.
🔗 Read more: https://sgom.es/posts/2026-02-13-js-heavy-approaches-are-not-compatible-with-long-term-performance-goals/
